headline: Corn dips 3¢ to $4.53, beans lose 16¢ to $12.40
lead: Soybeans gave back 16 cents overnight to $12.40, and meal fell harder at 1.8%, while corn barely moved at $4.53. Beans are carrying the grain market lower today. The 16 cents is a November futures move; what it means for beans in the bin depends on your local bid and basis. (Corrected Oct 27, see the note below.)
teaser: Corn eases to $4.53, beans slip 16 cents, and Crop Progress is due at 3 p.m. CT.

one_number.context: AgWeb says payments hit a record this year, with $8 diesel aid expected in November.

sections.title: Beans lead grains lower
sections.body:
- Soybeans are at **$12.40¼** overnight, down 1.3%, and meal is down 1.8% to $340.00.
- Corn eased 3 cents to $4.53 after Friday's modest trade, and wheat is up 1 cent at $6.26.
- Feedstuffs says larger inventories and high freight costs are straining grain merchandisers' working capital.
sections.so_what: Meal is pulling the bean move, not oil.

sections.title: Cattle hold near highs
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled Friday at **$229.875**, up 0.1%, and feeders gained 0.6% to $348.325.
- USDA's October Cattle on Feed showed September placements down 12%, the lowest for the month in the series.
sections.so_what: Thin placements are backing the feeder market.

sections.title: Crude slips; gas gains
sections.body:
- WTI is at **$101.14** overnight, down 2.1% from $103.27, though it holds above $100 on Houthi and Iranian attacks.
- Natural gas is up 13.9% to $3.01, and Europe's gas price is at a four-year high with Qatar's LNG still offline.
sections.so_what: Gas ran harder than crude on winter supply worry.

outside_the_pit.title: Diesel aid expected in November
outside_the_pit.body: AgWeb quotes Fordyce saying $8 diesel aid is coming in November, as government payments reach a record $55.4 billion.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress. Harvest pace shows how much corn and bean supply is reaching the bins.
Beans back above Friday's (Oct 23) $12.56½ settle would erase this overnight drop.
WTI under $100 would show Gulf supply fears easing; Brent above $114 says they are not.

source_summary: CME Group, USDA, AgWeb, Feedstuffs, OilPrice.com, Drovers

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.82 vs $4.62 projected (+4.3%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.74 vs $11.09 projected (+14.9%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 23, figured the way USDA RMA does. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 25. Oct 1-31 window, most states.

facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, last posted bid per trading day (data/bids-prev)

corrections.text: The opening said "A bushel of beans is worth about 16 cents less than it was at Friday's close." A futures move alone does not show what stored beans are worth; a cash bid also moves with local basis. November soybean futures traded at $12.40¼ at 5:45 a.m. CT Monday, 16¼ cents below Friday's $12.56½ settle.
